questions.question: The demo's 50-question evaluation set splits 30/12/8 by source. What are the three sources?
options: 30 real tickets, 12 edge cases, 8 adversarial cases
30 edge cases, 12 real tickets, 8 adversarial cases
30 adversarial cases, 12 edge cases, 8 real tickets
questions.explanation: See the "The evaluation set: three sources and rot-free upkeep" section: the three sources are real cases, edge cases, and adversarial cases — the demo's 50 questions split 30/12/8; every question must carry a golden answer and a class label to be scalable.

questions.question: Ordered by determinism, the three automated grading methods listed in the body are exact match, rule validation, and LLM-as-judge. Which of the following is NOT one of them?
options: Exact match (field values, enums, numbers compared directly)
Rule validation (parseable JSON, compliant dates, required-field presence)
questions.explanation: See the "Three automated scoring methods" section: the three moves are exact match, rule validation, and LLM-as-judge, ordered by determinism; "token-billing check" is a cost-engineering (G02) concern, not a grading method.

questions.question: What was the metric movement when v2's regression was caught?
options: The total fell from 0.88 to 0.82, and the billing class fell from 0.9 to 0.7
The total rose from 0.82 to 0.88, but the returns class fell from 0.9 to 0.7
The total fell from 0.94 to 0.88, and the billing class fell from 0.8 to 0.7
The total rose from 0.82 to 0.94, and all three subclasses passed
questions.explanation: See the "Regression testing: full re-runs are the discipline" section: v2's total rose from 0.82 to 0.88, and the returns class fell from 0.9 to 0.7 — the format of the newly added billing examples got imitated by the returns class, and a required field was dropped; an evaluation reading only the total lets this regression walk.
